raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Status

Superseded by the following Qwen3.8 Flash-Next draft stack:

- [1/n Add Flash-Next model, FSDP and checkpoint reference coverage](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5782)
- [2/n Add tensor and expert parallelism with batched QSA teachers](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5783)
- [3/n Honor deterministic GDN normalization](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5784)
- [4/n Add pipeline stages, remat and numerical integration coverage](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5785)

The original branch and local worktree are retained for reference.
The description below records the earlier implementation and its validation.

## Summary

Add the released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next text and vision backbone, following the `add_model` workflow proposed in #5636.

- Add `qwen3_8_flash_next` with the released `125B-A6B` configuration and an eight-layer debug configuration.
- Implement four gated residual streams (GR), per-layer lexical embeddings (PLE), and Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA), including the sparse-stage indexer KL objective.
- Add HF checkpoint conversion, reference parity checks, CPU feature tests, combined distributed training fixtures, and a committed deterministic numerical golden with an independent remote replay.

## Architectural choices

Flash-Next uses 48 decoder layers, dimension 2560, and a 3:1 Gated DeltaNet/QSA layout. It adds four residual streams, a learned block indexer, and a large n-gram lexical lookup table to the existing Qwen architecture. These components need model-specific equations and checkpoint mappings.

The port reuses Qwen3.5's Gated DeltaNet, expert computation and dispatch, vision encoder, multimodal preprocessing, MRoPE, and training lifecycle. The model-specific MoE adapters preserve HF's BF16 router rounding. Shared embedding, normalization, and RoPE options preserve existing defaults and checkpoint layouts.

PLE resets at EOS and packed document boundaries. Original token IDs and document positions survive pipeline boundaries independently of multimodal rotary coordinates. The lexical table uses TP across features, preserving HF row-chunk export without gathering the full table on each rank.

QSA selects complete four-token blocks causally and includes the current partial block. The training target sums detached main-attention probabilities across heads, max-pools complete blocks, and normalizes over selected blocks. TP heads are summed before pooling. The report does not give a loss coefficient; this configuration uses `1.0`, independently of the MoE load-balancing coefficient `0.001`.

Strict deterministic training exposed GDN L2-normalization backward autotuning choosing different FP32 reduction orders across fresh processes. The shared chunk, CP, and recomputed backward paths now disable this autotuning when strict determinism is enabled, matching KDA's existing policy. Normal-mode autotuning is preserved. The reference parity report and nine shared GDN GPU forward/backward tests pass with this change.

## Sources and checkpoint compatibility

- [Official HF checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next/tree/de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540), revision `de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540`.
- [Transformers Qwen4Exp reference](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/tree/494470d677d05d44153d235d795e0d01040307ab/src/transformers/models/qwen4_exp), revision `494470d677d05d44153d235d795e0d01040307ab`.
- [Architecture study](https://shuhuayu.github.io/studies/qwen3-8-flash-next.html).

The adapter covers all 1,627 backbone/vision checkpoint entries and warns about the 31 unused `mtp.*` entries. Reduced checkpoint round trips load strictly; the complete released checkpoint schema is checked using meta tensors. Native parameter accounting is 177,392,830,576, including the 51,200,245,760-parameter lexical table and 448,931,056-parameter vision encoder. The flavor name follows the release's `125B-A6B` label.

## Validation

The recorded runtime evidence uses source base `72a3a126fe732317d1ebaecab566933dca769758`, PyTorch `2.16.0.dev20261006+cu132`, seed 42, and strict deterministic execution. The reports record software, input, tokenizer, initialization, and source provenance.

- `pre-commit run --all-files`: all hooks passed, including a fresh run before opening this draft.
- 146 targeted CPU tests passed: independent functional oracles, gradients, packed boundaries, model/config contracts, checkpoint conversion, shared components, auxiliary-loss resets, and integration-recipe registration.
- Nine shared GDN GPU forward/backward tests passed in strict deterministic mode.
- Ten-step plain/remat runs matched every full-precision TensorBoard loss and grad_norm exactly.
- A real eight-GPU GB200 TorchX/MAST run completed ten steps with **FSDP2 + TP2 + EP4 + PP2**, sequence parallelism, 1F1B, two microbatches, and PLE on the second pipeline stage.
- Separate PP2 and multimodal runs completed ten steps. The image fixture uses sequence length 1024 and exercises the vision encoder.
- A 100-step reduced-model run on C4 English with the pinned official tokenizer reduced mean loss from **12.507574** (steps 1-10) to **7.963772** (steps 91-100). These convergence values use stdout rounded to five decimal places.

### Same-weight reference parity

| Comparison | Maximum absolute error |
| --- | --- |
| GR forward, input and parameter gradients, FP32 | 0 |
| PLE forward, FP32 | 7.45e-9 |
| PLE input and parameter gradients, FP32 | 3.19e-12 |
| QSA forward, FP32 | 4.10e-8 |
| Vision including merger, FP32 | 3.28e-7 |
| Full eight-layer logits, BF16 | 0.001953125 |

The BF16 fixture selects identical experts at every layer. Logit cosine similarity is `0.9999963898`; mean per-token KL(reference || native) is `8.10e-8`; top-1 and top-5 sets agree for every fixture token. The reproducible harness and checked-in report are:

- `scripts/checkpoint_conversion/numerical_tests_qwen3_8_flash_next.py`
- `tests/assets/numerics/qwen3_8_flash_next_reference.json`

Packed BF16 routing has two near-tied tokens whose expert sets differ from separate document invocations, with maximum logit error `0.02587890625`. Replaying isolated expert IDs while recomputing packed mixing weights reduces the maximum error to `0.00390625`. Independent CPU boundary tests verify the underlying math; unconstrained packed BF16 routing is not bitwise equivalent in this fixture.

### Deterministic remote golden

Two independent fresh GB200 launches completed ten TP2/EP2/SP steps with identical full-precision loss and grad_norm before golden export. The registered integration runner then exported the golden. A subsequent independent launch imported the committed golden without export and passed exact loss and grad_norm assertions at every step.

- Golden: `tests/assets/losses/real_pg/qwen3_8_flash_next_gb200.txt`
- Registered B200 test: `qwen3_8_flash_next_tp_ep_numerics`
- H100 suite fixtures: combined parallelism, PP2, activation remat, and multimodal training.

```bash
python -m tests.integration_tests.run_tests outputs/flash-next-replay \
  --test_suite b200 --test_name qwen3_8_flash_next_tp_ep_numerics \
  --execution_mode real_pg --gpu_arch_type cuda --gpu_arch b200 \
  --ngpu 2 --no-parallel
```

The model README and golden header contain the remote job IDs, persistent output paths, and complete replay provenance.

## Execution limits

- QSA uses bounded gather/indexer chunks and native SDPA MATH. Dynamic selection shapes currently require disabling CUDA graphs; context parallelism is explicitly rejected.
- MTP training and speculative decoding are outside the port's current scope.
- Full 177B parameter materialization, production-scale convergence, and production throughput have not been validated.
- The pinned nightly has a preexisting CosSinRoPE eager/compile discrepancy on unchanged upstream/main: one BF16 gradient value differs by `9.54e-7`. The pinned CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2 supports the validated fused GDN backend; the optional cuDNN backend requires DSL 4.7.0.

## Draft follow-ups for current upstream/main

The two implementation commits were validated against the source base above. Latest upstream/main (`3f990a8e9` when this draft was prepared) merges without textual conflicts, but has since changed the compile configuration and loss contracts.

- [ ] Migrate the Flash-Next configuration and fixtures from `local_compile_regions` to `LocalCompileConfig`, following #5463, so the intended eager debug configuration is honored.
- [ ] Revalidate the integration fixtures and deterministic golden on current upstream/main, including the compile configuration update and loss abstraction redesign in #4582, before marking this PR ready for review.

nodes.body:
**Claude finished @shuhuayu's task in 3m 12s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/40969355097)

---
**Request changes** -- see the [review](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5655#pullrequestreview).

**Verdict: Request changes** -- The model port is the right thing to add, but it changes shared code (three single-consumer flags, plus a GDN determinism fix for every GDN model), lets the indexer KL train the backbone with a coefficient that isn't sourced, and commits internal-infra provenance to OSS files.

**What this PR does.** Adds `qwen3_8_flash_next`, a subclass of Qwen3.5. It adds three things:
- four gated residual streams, carried as one `[T, 4*D]` tensor;
- a hashed n-gram lexical table (PLE) on layer 1, TP-sharded by feature;
- QSA, where each query attends to the top-k 4-token blocks plus its own partial block, and an indexer is distilled from detached main-attention probabilities via `AuxLoss.inject`.

It also changes `common/embedding.py`, `common/norm.py`, `common/rope.py` and `common/attention/{gdn,cp_gdn}.py`, and adds five integration entries with a B200 golden.

**Example.** For a packed document at token 9 with `compress_ratio=4` and `token_budget=4` (one block):
```
complete blocks: [0..3] ends at 3, [4..7] ends at 7 -> visible (end <= 9, same doc)
indexer scores both, picks top-1, e.g. [4..7]
tail: token 8 and 9 (local_count % 4 = 2 -> current partial block)
SDPA over J = [4,5,6,7,8,9]; KL target = max-pool over heads-summed probs of [4..7]
```
Today, gradients of that KL reach `x_TD` and every layer below it. In DeepSeek V4's equivalent, they stop at the indexer.

### Must fix
1. `tests/assets/losses/real_pg/qwen3_8_flash_next_gb200.txt:1-43` and `torchtitan/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/README.md:125-185` -- These files contain MAST job IDs, `metaconda`/`torchx` images and Manifold paths under a username. The README also narrates validation history ("previously chose", "the original MAST image predates..."). Move both to the PR description. The README should describe the architecture, the supported and verified parallelisms, and the HF numerics check.
2. `torchtitan/models/common/embedding.py:31`, `common/norm.py:30`, `common/rope.py:390` -- Three boolean flags in shared modules, each set only by Flash-Next. Move them into model-folder subclasses, or make the HF rounding the single behavior if it matches the reference for Qwen3.5 too (see inline comments).
3. `torchtitan/models/common/attention/gdn.py:125-126` -- The GDN l2norm autotune change is a separate concern that touches every GDN model. The recurrent path is changed unconditionally, which contradicts the description and may break trainer/generator parity. Split it into its own PR.
4. `torchtitan/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/attention.py:325-331` -- The indexer input isn't detached, so indexer-KL gradients train the backbone, and `coeff=1.0` (`flavors.py:236`) has no source. Detach the input as DSV4 does, or cite the report.
5. `torchtitan/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/model.py:120` -- The production flavor compiles nothing by default, including `loss` and the norm regions, and nothing explains why. Inherit Qwen3.5's default when migrating to `LocalCompileConfig` (#5463), which the description already lists as a follow-up.
6. `tests/integration_tests/h100.py:188-219` -- Four new H100 entries. `pp2` is a subset of `all_parallelism`, and `ac` and `mm` can be merged. Prefer an interleaved schedule with spmd typechecking in the combined entry.
7. `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/test_qwen3_8_flash_next.py:499-590` -- These tests only re-read recipe and golden config. Delete them.
8. `tests/assets/numerics/qwen3_8_flash_next_reference.json` -- A 374-line report that no test reads. The script writes to `outputs/` by default. Keep the summary in the PR description and drop the file from `tests/assets/`.

### Should consider
- `torchtitan/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/attention.py:241-285, 111-148` -- Each QSA layer runs a per-chunk TP all-reduce (about 16k at the flavor's 262k context) and recomputes the block metadata with `.nonzero()` syncs. Do one all-reduce per forward and add a TODO for a sparse kernel. Enabling CUDA graphs should fail clearly instead of at capture.
- `torchtitan/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/attention.py:209-212,322` -- `build_attention_metadata` builds varlen metadata every step, and `forward` then discards it.
- `torchtitan/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/moe.py:31` -- `.to(input.dtype).float()` is the round trip that Inductor drops (`hi_mid_lo_linear.py:413`). Under compile, the HF-matching router rounding may silently disappear.
- `torchtitan/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/flavors.py:369-373` -- `attn_backend` accepts only its own default and raises otherwise. Drop the parameter.
- `torchtitan/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/model.py:213-222` -- `document_positions` and `ple_input_ids` fall back silently, but `preprocess_inputs` always supplies both. Remove the fallbacks.
- `torchtitan/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/state_dict_adapter.py:89,119` -- `chunk`/`cat` along dim 0 of the 51B-row table, which FSDP shards on dim 0, may redistribute across DP. The same applies to FSDP unsharding the table on every forward at full scale (unverified). This bears on the README's "without gathering" claim.

### Questions
- Was the GB200-recorded golden checked on the B200 CI runner the suite actually uses?
- Does the report specify whether the indexer KL should back-propagate into the backbone?

Not verified: GPU numerics, l2norm forward rounding under autotune, DTensor redistribution in the adapter. A maintainer still needs to review, since this touches `models/common/`.

This header names internal infrastructure in an OSS file:
- MAST hosts (line 4)
- `metaconda_demo:` workspaces (lines 8, 41)
- `torchx_base_conda_env` (line 12)
- MAST job IDs (lines 36, 38, 40)
- Manifold paths under a personal username (lines 39, 43)

External contributors can't use any of it, and none of it is needed to replay the golden. Sibling goldens such as `kimi_k3_b200.txt` keep a header of about 4 lines: config, ngpu, parallelism, hardware. Trim the header to that and put the provenance in the PR description.

Related question: the golden was recorded on GB200 hosts, but the registered suite runs on B200 CI runners. Has a B200 run been checked to reproduce these values bit for bit?

This adds a boolean mode switch to the shared `Embedding`, and its only consumer is the Flash-Next n-gram table (`flavors.py:139`). It also forces the edit in `transformers_modeling_backend/module_conversion.py`.

`.claude/rules/config.md` says implementations are selected by config type, not by a boolean. Core principle 4 says shared modules shouldn't be bent for one model.

`NGramEmbedding` already owns the table's sharding (`ngram_table_sharding`, TP `S(1)`). It can hold a plain `nn.Embedding` (or call `F.embedding` on its own parameter) inside `qwen3_8_flash_next/embedding.py`. That would leave `common/embedding.py` and `module_conversion.py` unchanged.

- **If no:** keep the variant in the model folder as a subclass, as `moe.py` already does for `RouterLinear` and `FlashNextRouter`.

Either way, `common/norm.py` and `common/rope.py` shouldn't gain flags that only one model sets.

nodes.body:
On the recurrent path, autotuning is disabled unconditionally, not only in deterministic mode. That contradicts the description's "normal-mode autotuning is preserved".

This path exists so the trainer's forward is bitwise identical to the vLLM generator. The generator still calls `l2norm(query, cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens)` with default autotuning (`rl/generator/vllm/gdn.py:323-324`). If l2norm's forward tile choice affects rounding, trainer/generator parity breaks (unverified).

More broadly, this GDN determinism change affects every GDN model (qwen3_5/6/8, RL) and fixes a pre-existing issue that isn't specific to Flash-Next. It also carries renames (`normalized_q` -> `normalized_q_BTHK`, the `B = batch` legend).

Please split it into its own PR, with:
- the problem shown on main (a fresh-process mismatch for qwen3_5);
- a check that the deterministic goldens of existing GDN models are unchanged, or regenerated with an explanation;
- the recurrent call sites either left alone or matched on both the trainer and generator sides.

nodes.body:
The indexer receives a non-detached `x_TD`, so the indexer-KL gradient flows into the residual streams, the hyper-connections and every earlier layer. The KL target is detached (`attention.py:259`); the student input is not.

DeepSeek V4, the existing sparse-indexer distillation in this repo, detaches the indexer inputs (`deepseek_v4/attention.py:392`: `self.indexer(x.detach(), qr.detach(), ...)`). With `coeff=1.0` (`flavors.py:236`, 100x DSV4's `0.01`) and no coefficient in the report, the KL can noticeably reshape backbone training.

Unless the Flash-Next report says the indexer loss should train the backbone, pass `x_TD.detach()` to the indexer here. Either way, state the choice and where `coeff=1.0` comes from in the flavor.

+# T = packed tokens, U = valid tokens, G = complete blocks, R = block size,
+# B = selected blocks, J = selected tokens including the incomplete tail,
+# H = query or KV heads, K = head dimension, V = value dimension,
+# D = model dimension, Q = query chunk, C = projection channels.
+
+
+class QSAIndexer(Module):
+    """Score average-pooled complete blocks; always keep the incomplete tail."""
+
+    @dataclass(kw_only=True, slots=True)
+    class Config(Module.Config):
+        num_heads: int
+        head_dim: int
+        rotary_dim: int
+        token_budget: int
+        compress_ratio: int
+        index_qk_proj: Linear.Config
+        q_layernorm: OffsetRMSNorm.Config
+        k_layernorm: OffsetRMSNorm.Config
+        rope: MRoPE.Config
+        chunk_size: int = 128
+
+        def __post_init__(self):
+            if (
+                min(self.num_heads, self.head_dim, self.compress_ratio, self.chunk_size)
+                <= 0
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "Indexer head counts, dimensions and chunk sizes must be positive"
+                )
+            if (
+                self.token_budget < self.compress_ratio
+                or self.token_budget % self.compress_ratio
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "token_budget must be a positive multiple of compress_ratio"
+                )
+            if not 0 < self.rotary_dim <= self.head_dim or self.rotary_dim % 2:
+                raise ValueError("rotary_dim must be positive, even and <= head_dim")
+
+    def __init__(self, config: Config):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.num_heads = config.num_heads
+        self.head_dim = config.head_dim
+        self.rotary_dim = config.rotary_dim
+        self.compress_ratio = config.compress_ratio
+        self.block_topk = config.token_budget // config.compress_ratio
+        self.chunk_size = config.chunk_size
+        self.index_qk_proj = config.index_qk_proj.build()
+        self.q_layernorm = config.q_layernorm.build()
+        self.k_layernorm = config.k_layernorm.build()
+        self.rope = config.rope.build()
+
+    def _rotate(self, x_THK: torch.Tensor, positions_T: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        rotary_THR = x_THK[..., : self.rotary_dim]
+        rotary_THR, _ = self.rope(rotary_THR, rotary_THR, positions_T)
+        return torch.cat((rotary_THR, x_THK[..., self.rotary_dim :]), -1)

+        self,
+        x_TD: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        document_positions_T: torch.Tensor,
+        padding_mask_T: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        num_tokens = x_TD.shape[0]
+        qk_TC = self.index_qk_proj(x_TD)
+        remat.recompute_needs_tensor(qk_TC)
+        query_TC, raw_key_TK = qk_TC.split(
+            (self.num_heads * self.head_dim, self.head_dim), -1
+        )
+        query_THK = self._rotate(
+            self.q_layernorm(query_TC.unflatten(-1, (self.num_heads, self.head_dim))),
+            positions,
+        )
+        indices_T = torch.arange(num_tokens, device=x_TD.device)
+        starts_T = document_starts(document_positions_T)
+        valid_T = (
+            torch.ones_like(indices_T, dtype=torch.bool)
+            if padding_mask_T is None
+            else ~padding_mask_T
+        )
+        counts_T = valid_T.long().cumsum(0)
+        start_counts_T = F.pad(counts_T[:-1], (1, 0))[starts_T]
+        local_counts_T = counts_T - start_counts_T
+        valid_indices_U = valid_T.nonzero().flatten()
+        block_ends_G = (
+            (valid_T & (local_counts_T.remainder(self.compress_ratio) == 0))
+            .nonzero()
+            .flatten()
+        )
+        block_indices_GR = valid_indices_U[
+            counts_T[block_ends_G, None]
+            - self.compress_ratio
+            + torch.arange(self.compress_ratio, device=x_TD.device)
+        ]
+        pooled_GK = raw_key_TK[block_indices_GR].float().mean(1).to(raw_key_TK.dtype)
+        key_GK = self._rotate(
+            self.k_layernorm(pooled_GK).unsqueeze(1), positions[block_indices_GR[:, 0]]
+        ).squeeze(1)

+        tail_count_T = local_counts_T.remainder(self.compress_ratio)
+        tail_offsets_TR = torch.arange(
+            self.compress_ratio - 1, device=x_TD.device
+        ).expand(num_tokens, -1)
+        tail_slots_TR = counts_T[:, None] - tail_count_T[:, None] + tail_offsets_TR
+        # The extra entry makes all-padding documents a well-defined empty selection.
+        tail_indices_TR = F.pad(valid_indices_U, (0, 1))[
+            tail_slots_TR.clamp_max(valid_indices_U.numel())
+        ]

+        self.indexer_loss = config.indexer_loss.build()

+        key_THK: torch.Tensor,
+        value_THV: torch.Tensor,

+                ).squeeze(2)

+                        query_QH1K.shape[1] // keys_QHJK.shape[1], 1
+                    )

+                    ) * scale

+                    )

+                        )

+                    # changes the target distribution.

+                        .unflatten(-1, (num_blocks, self.compress_ratio))
+                        .amax(-1)
+                    )

+            )
+            output_THV = self.indexer_loss.inject(
+                raw_sum,
+                carrier=output_THV,
+                denominator=aux_loss_denominator,

+            positions=positions,
+            document_positions_T=document_positions_T,
+            padding_mask_T=padding_mask_T,
+        )

This issues one TP `all_reduce` for every 16-query chunk. With the flavor's 262144 context, that is about 16k collectives plus 16k SDPA-MATH calls per QSA layer per microbatch. The surrounding loop does the same work in Python.

The block metadata at lines 111-148 (`document_starts`, `.nonzero()` x2, `num_selected` from `.numel()`) is recomputed in all 12 QSA layers. It depends only on `document_positions`/`padding_mask`, and each call adds device-to-host syncs.

Smallest improvements:
- Collect `teacher_QJ` across chunks and all-reduce once per forward, as `SparseIndexerLoss` does in `deepseek_v4/compressor.py`.
- Add a TODO that the gather+MATH path is a placeholder for a sparse kernel.

Also, this code can't be CUDA-graph captured, but only the recipes set `disable_cuda_graphs`. A user who enables CUDA graphs gets a capture failure instead of a `ValueError`.

This re-declares the base field with an empty default, so the `125B-A6B` flavor runs every local-compile region eagerly, including `loss`, `gated_rmsnorm`, `offset_rmsnorm` and `partial_rope`. Its parent `Qwen35Model.Config` compiles all of those by default (`qwen3_5/model.py:337`).

There's no comment explaining the change. The production flavor would silently get slower than its Qwen3.5 sibling.

The field is also the stale API that #5463 replaced with `LocalCompileConfig`, as the description notes. When migrating, inherit Qwen3.5's default. If a region genuinely can't compile for this model, drop only that region and add a comment explaining why.

Four new H100 entries for one model is more CI than the coverage needs (`.claude/rules/tests.md`):
- `qwen3_8_flash_next_pp2` (PP2, PLE on stage 2) is a strict subset of `qwen3_8_flash_next_all_parallelism`. Drop it.
- `_ac` and `_mm` are both 1-GPU runs. Fold them into one entry (remat plus images), or enable remat in `all_parallelism`.
- `all_parallelism` uses 1F1B with no SPMD type checking. Switching to an interleaved schedule with `spmd_typechecking=True` covers the harder configuration at no extra cost.

That gives one 8-GPU entry and at most one 1-GPU entry.

+    for token, position in zip(ids.tolist(), positions.tolist()):
+        if position == 0:

+        context = [token, *(history[::-1][:2])]

+def test_qsa_selection_matches_document_local_block_oracle(config):
+    torch.manual_seed(42)

+    x = torch.randn(39, 256)
+    positions = torch.cat((torch.arange(19), torch.arange(20)))

+    padding[5] = padding[37:] = True
+    selected, scores = indexer(
+        x, positions=positions, document_positions_T=positions, padding_mask_T=padding
+    )
+    projection = indexer.index_qk_proj(x)
+    queries = indexer._rotate(
+        indexer.q_layernorm(projection[:, :256].unflatten(-1, (4, 64))), positions
+    )
+    for query in range(39):
+        begin = 0 if query < 19 else 19
+        visible = (
+            [token for token in range(begin, query + 1) if not padding[token]]
+            if not padding[query]
+            else []
+        )
+        complete = len(visible) // 4
+        blocks = torch.tensor(visible[: complete * 4], dtype=torch.long).reshape(

+def test_router_bfloat16_ties_mixing_and_backward(config):
+    """Round before expert selection and retain differentiable normalized gates."""
+    router = config.layers[3].feed_forward.router.build().bfloat16().eval()
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        router.gate.weight.zero_()
+        router.gate.weight[0, :2] = torch.tensor([1.0, 1 / 256])
+        router.gate.weight[1, 0] = 1

+    reference_weight = router.gate.weight.detach().float().requires_grad_()
+    reference_x = x.detach().float().requires_grad_()
+    logits = F.linear(reference_x, reference_weight).to(x.dtype).float()
+    reference_scores, reference_ids = logits.softmax(-1).topk(2, -1)
+    reference_scores = (reference_scores / reference_scores.sum(-1, keepdim=True)).to(
+        x.dtype
+    )
+    scores, indices, routing = router(x)
+    expected_routing = torch.zeros_like(logits, dtype=torch.bool).scatter(
+        -1, reference_ids, True
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(routing, expected_routing)
+    assert not torch.equal(
+        indices.sort(-1).values,
+        F.linear(reference_x, reference_weight).topk(2, -1).indices.sort(-1).values,
+    )
+    actual_weights = torch.zeros_like(logits).scatter(-1, indices, scores.float())
+    expected_weights = torch.zeros_like(logits).scatter(
+        -1, reference_ids, reference_scores.float()
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_weights, expected_weights, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    objective = torch.arange(8, dtype=torch.float32)
+    actual_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
+        (actual_weights * objective).sum(), (x, router.gate.weight)
+    )
+    expected_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
+        (expected_weights * objective).sum(), (reference_x, reference_weight)
+    )
+    for actual_grad, expected_grad in zip(actual_gradients, expected_gradients):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            actual_grad.float(), expected_grad.to(x.dtype).float(), atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-2
+        )
+
+
+def test_adapter_roundtrip_and_numeric_shard_order(config):
+    model = config.build()
+    model.init_states()
+    adapter = Qwen38FlashNextStateDictAdapter(config, None)
+    state = model.state_dict()
+    hf = adapter.to_hf(state)
+    restored = adapter.from_hf(dict(reversed(list(hf.items()))))
+    assert restored.keys() == state.keys()
+    for key in state:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(restored[key], state[key], rtol=0, atol=0, msg=key)
+    config.build().load_state_dict(restored, strict=True)
+    shard = next(key for key in hf if ".shard_0." in key)
+    del hf[shard]
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="requires all"):
+        adapter.from_hf(hf)
+
+
+def test_original_ids_and_gradients_survive_a_pipeline_split(config):
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    config.layers = [copy.deepcopy(config.layers[3]), copy.deepcopy(config.layers[1])]
+    config.layers[1].attention = copy.deepcopy(config.layers[0].attention)
+    full = config.build().eval()
+    full.init_states()
+    first, last = copy.deepcopy(full), copy.deepcopy(full)
+    del first.layers["1"]
+    first.norm = first.lm_head = first.hyper_connection_mixer = None
+    del last.layers["0"]
+    last.tok_embeddings = None
+    ids = torch.randint(0, 63, (25,))
+    positions = torch.cat((torch.arange(11), torch.arange(14)))
+    expected = full(ids, positions=positions)
+    hidden = first(ids, positions=positions)
+    actual = last(
+        hidden, positions=positions, ple_input_ids=ids, document_positions=positions
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    actual.square().mean().backward()
+    expected.square().mean().backward()
+    for stage in (first, last):
+        for name, parameter in stage.named_parameters():
+            # Splitting the graph can reorder FP32 gradient additions.
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                parameter.grad,
+                dict(full.named_parameters())[name].grad,
+                rtol=1e-5,
+                atol=1e-7,
+                msg=lambda message: f"{name}: {message}",
+            )
+
+
+def test_optimizer_resets_auxiliary_losses_once_with_remat(config):
+    from torchtitan.distributed.activation_remat import FullActivationRematConfig
+    from torchtitan.models.common.aux_loss import AuxLoss
+    from torchtitan.models.qwen3_8_flash_next.model import Qwen38FlashNextModel
+
+    config.layers = [copy.deepcopy(config.layers[3]), copy.deepcopy(config.layers[1])]
+    config.layers[1].attention = copy.deepcopy(config.layers[0].attention)
+    saved_counts, saved_acc = AuxLoss._group_counts.copy(), AuxLoss.group_acc.copy()
+    try:
+        for use_remat in (False, True):
+            torch.manual_seed(42)
+            model = config.build()
+            model.init_states()
+            if use_remat:
+                FullActivationRematConfig().apply(model)
+            optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0)
+            Qwen38FlashNextModel._register_optimizer_hooks(optimizer, [model], None)
+            losses = [
+                module
+                for module in model.modules()
+                if isinstance(module, QSAIndexerLoss)
+            ]
+            ids, positions = torch.randint(0, 63, (23,)), torch.arange(23)
+            for _ in range(2):
+                output = model(
+                    ids, positions=positions, aux_loss_denominators=torch.tensor([46.0])
+                )
+                accumulated = [loss.instance_acc.clone() for loss in losses]
+                output.square().mean().backward()
+                for loss, expected in zip(losses, accumulated):
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(
+                        loss.instance_acc, expected, atol=0, rtol=0
+                    )
+            expected = sum(loss.instance_acc.clone() for loss in losses)
+            assert expected > 0
+            optimizer.step()
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                AuxLoss.group_acc[("loss", "qsa_indexer_loss")],
+                expected,
+                atol=0,
+                rtol=0,
+            )
+            assert all(loss.instance_acc == 0 for loss in losses)
+            optimizer.step()
+            assert AuxLoss.group_acc[("loss", "qsa_indexer_loss")] == 0
+    finally:
+        AuxLoss._group_counts.clear()
+        AuxLoss._group_counts.update(saved_counts)
+        AuxLoss.group_acc.clear()
+        AuxLoss.group_acc.update(saved_acc)
+
+
+def test_integration_recipe_and_pipeline_placement():
+    from torchtitan.distributed.pipeline_parallel import (
+        _generate_llm_fqn_per_model_part,
+    )
+    from torchtitan.models.common.decoder import TransformerBlock
+    from torchtitan.models.qwen3_8_flash_next.model import Qwen38FlashNextModel
+
+    from tests.integration_tests.h100 import build_h100_tests_list
+
+    test = next(
+        test
+        for test in build_h100_tests_list()
+        if test.test_name == "qwen3_8_flash_next_all_parallelism"
+    )
+    cfg = test.configs[0]()
+    assert test.ngpu == 8 and test.use_real_pg
+    assert isinstance(cfg.model, Qwen38FlashNextModel.Config)
+    assert all(isinstance(layer, TransformerBlock.Config) for layer in cfg.model.layers)
+    parallelism = cfg.parallelism
+    assert (
+        parallelism.data_parallel_shard_degree,
+        parallelism.tensor_parallel_degree,
+        parallelism.expert_parallel_degree,
+        parallelism.pipeline_parallel_degree,
+    ) == (2, 2, 4, 2)
+    assert parallelism.num_pp_microbatches == 2 and cfg.training.steps >= 10
+    assert (
+        cfg.debug.seed == 42
+        and cfg.debug.deterministic
+        and not cfg.debug.deterministic_warn_only
+    )
+    stages = _generate_llm_fqn_per_model_part(
+        2,
+        8,
+        parallelism.pipeline_parallel_first_stage_less_layers,
+        parallelism.pipeline_parallel_last_stage_less_layers,
+    )
+    assert "layers.1" not in stages[0] and "layers.1" in stages[1]
+
+
+def test_numerical_recipe_and_golden_retain_model_features():
+    from torchtitan_recipes.tests.models.qwen3_8_flash_next import (
+        qwen38_flash_next_debugmodel,
+        qwen38_flash_next_debugmodel_tp2,
+    )
+
+    from tests.integration_tests.b200 import build_b200_tests_list
+
+    test = next(
+        test
+        for test in build_b200_tests_list()
+        if test.test_name == "qwen3_8_flash_next_tp_ep_numerics"
+    )
+    assert list(test.configs) == [qwen38_flash_next_debugmodel_tp2]
+    assert test.loss_compare_seed_config is qwen38_flash_next_debugmodel
+    assert test.ngpu == 2 and test.use_real_pg and not test.disabled
+    cfg = test.configs[0]()
+    assert (
+        cfg.parallelism.tensor_parallel_degree,
+        cfg.parallelism.expert_parallel_degree,
+        cfg.parallelism.pipeline_parallel_degree,
+        cfg.parallelism.context_parallel_degree,
+    ) == (2, 2, 1, 1)
+    assert cfg.parallelism.enable_sequence_parallel and cfg.debug.spmd_typechecking
+    assert cfg.debug.seed == 42 and cfg.debug.deterministic
+    assert not cfg.debug.deterministic_warn_only
+    assert cfg.training.steps >= 10 and cfg.training.disable_cuda_graphs
+    assert cfg.activation_remat is None and not cfg.model.local_compile_regions
+    assert cfg.model.num_streams == 4 and cfg.model.layers[1].ple is not None
+    assert any(isinstance(layer.attention, GDN.Config) for layer in cfg.model.layers)
+    sparse_layers = [
+        layer
+        for layer in cfg.model.layers
+        if isinstance(layer.attention, QSAAttention.Config)
+    ]
+    assert sparse_layers and all(
+        isinstance(layer.feed_forward, MoE.Config) for layer in cfg.model.layers
+    )
+    assert all(
+        layer.attention.indexer.token_budget < cfg.training.max_context_length
+        for layer in sparse_layers
+    )
+    assert test.golden_numerics_path is not None
+    golden = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / test.golden_numerics_path
+    lines = golden.read_text().splitlines()
+    assert "# step loss grad_norm" in lines
+    rows = [line.split() for line in lines if line.strip() and not line.startswith("#")]
+    assert [int(row[0]) for row in rows] == list(range(1, 11))
+    assert all(
+        len(row) == 3 and all(math.isfinite(float(value)) for value in row[1:])
+        for row in rows
+    )

detail.body:
## Status

Superseded by the following Qwen3.8 Flash-Next draft stack:

- [1/n Add Flash-Next model, FSDP and checkpoint reference coverage](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5782)
- [2/n Add tensor and expert parallelism with batched QSA teachers](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5783)
- [3/n Honor deterministic GDN normalization](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5784)
- [4/n Add pipeline stages, remat and numerical integration coverage](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5785)

The original branch and local worktree are retained for reference.
The description below records the earlier implementation and its validation.

## Summary

Add the released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next text and vision backbone, following the `add_model` workflow proposed in #5636.

- Add `qwen3_8_flash_next` with the released `125B-A6B` configuration and an eight-layer debug configuration.
- Implement four gated residual streams (GR), per-layer lexical embeddings (PLE), and Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA), including the sparse-stage indexer KL objective.
- Add HF checkpoint conversion, reference parity checks, CPU feature tests, combined distributed training fixtures, and a committed deterministic numerical golden with an independent remote replay.

## Architectural choices

Flash-Next uses 48 decoder layers, dimension 2560, and a 3:1 Gated DeltaNet/QSA layout. It adds four residual streams, a learned block indexer, and a large n-gram lexical lookup table to the existing Qwen architecture. These components need model-specific equations and checkpoint mappings.

The port reuses Qwen3.5's Gated DeltaNet, expert computation and dispatch, vision encoder, multimodal preprocessing, MRoPE, and training lifecycle. The model-specific MoE adapters preserve HF's BF16 router rounding. Shared embedding, normalization, and RoPE options preserve existing defaults and checkpoint layouts.

PLE resets at EOS and packed document boundaries. Original token IDs and document positions survive pipeline boundaries independently of multimodal rotary coordinates. The lexical table uses TP across features, preserving HF row-chunk export without gathering the full table on each rank.

QSA selects complete four-token blocks causally and includes the current partial block. The training target sums detached main-attention probabilities across heads, max-pools complete blocks, and normalizes over selected blocks. TP heads are summed before pooling. The report does not give a loss coefficient; this configuration uses `1.0`, independently of the MoE load-balancing coefficient `0.001`.

Strict deterministic training exposed GDN L2-normalization backward autotuning choosing different FP32 reduction orders across fresh processes. The shared chunk, CP, and recomputed backward paths now disable this autotuning when strict determinism is enabled, matching KDA's existing policy. Normal-mode autotuning is preserved. The reference parity report and nine shared GDN GPU forward/backward tests pass with this change.

## Sources and checkpoint compatibility

- [Official HF checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next/tree/de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540), revision `de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540`.
- [Transformers Qwen4Exp reference](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/tree/494470d677d05d44153d235d795e0d01040307ab/src/transformers/models/qwen4_exp), revision `494470d677d05d44153d235d795e0d01040307ab`.
- [Architecture study](https://shuhuayu.github.io/studies/qwen3-8-flash-next.html).

The adapter covers all 1,627 backbone/vision checkpoint entries and warns about the 31 unused `mtp.*` entries. Reduced checkpoint round trips load strictly; the complete released checkpoint schema is checked using meta tensors. Native parameter accounting is 177,392,830,576, including the 51,200,245,760-parameter lexical table and 448,931,056-parameter vision encoder. The flavor name follows the release's `125B-A6B` label.

## Validation

The recorded runtime evidence uses source base `72a3a126fe732317d1ebaecab566933dca769758`, PyTorch `2.16.0.dev20261006+cu132`, seed 42, and strict deterministic execution. The reports record software, input, tokenizer, initialization, and source provenance.

- `pre-commit run --all-files`: all hooks passed, including a fresh run before opening this draft.
- 146 targeted CPU tests passed: independent functional oracles, gradients, packed boundaries, model/config contracts, checkpoint conversion, shared components, auxiliary-loss resets, and integration-recipe registration.
- Nine shared GDN GPU forward/backward tests passed in strict deterministic mode.
- Ten-step plain/remat runs matched every full-precision TensorBoard loss and grad_norm exactly.
- A real eight-GPU GB200 TorchX/MAST run completed ten steps with **FSDP2 + TP2 + EP4 + PP2**, sequence parallelism, 1F1B, two microbatches, and PLE on the second pipeline stage.
- Separate PP2 and multimodal runs completed ten steps. The image fixture uses sequence length 1024 and exercises the vision encoder.
- A 100-step reduced-model run on C4 English with the pinned official tokenizer reduced mean loss from **12.507574** (steps 1-10) to **7.963772** (steps 91-100). These convergence values use stdout rounded to five decimal places.

### Same-weight reference parity

| Comparison | Maximum absolute error |
| --- | --- |
| GR forward, input and parameter gradients, FP32 | 0 |
| PLE forward, FP32 | 7.45e-9 |
| PLE input and parameter gradients, FP32 | 3.19e-12 |
| QSA forward, FP32 | 4.10e-8 |
| Vision including merger, FP32 | 3.28e-7 |
| Full eight-layer logits, BF16 | 0.001953125 |

The BF16 fixture selects identical experts at every layer. Logit cosine similarity is `0.9999963898`; mean per-token KL(reference || native) is `8.10e-8`; top-1 and top-5 sets agree for every fixture token. The reproducible harness and checked-in report are:

- `scripts/checkpoint_conversion/numerical_tests_qwen3_8_flash_next.py`
- `tests/assets/numerics/qwen3_8_flash_next_reference.json`

Packed BF16 routing has two near-tied tokens whose expert sets differ from separate document invocations, with maximum logit error `0.02587890625`. Replaying isolated expert IDs while recomputing packed mixing weights reduces the maximum error to `0.00390625`. Independent CPU boundary tests verify the underlying math; unconstrained packed BF16 routing is not bitwise equivalent in this fixture.

### Deterministic remote golden

Two independent fresh GB200 launches completed ten TP2/EP2/SP steps with identical full-precision loss and grad_norm before golden export. The registered integration runner then exported the golden. A subsequent independent launch imported the committed golden without export and passed exact loss and grad_norm assertions at every step.

- Golden: `tests/assets/losses/real_pg/qwen3_8_flash_next_gb200.txt`
- Registered B200 test: `qwen3_8_flash_next_tp_ep_numerics`
- H100 suite fixtures: combined parallelism, PP2, activation remat, and multimodal training.

```bash
python -m tests.integration_tests.run_tests outputs/flash-next-replay \
  --test_suite b200 --test_name qwen3_8_flash_next_tp_ep_numerics \
  --execution_mode real_pg --gpu_arch_type cuda --gpu_arch b200 \
  --ngpu 2 --no-parallel
```

The model README and golden header contain the remote job IDs, persistent output paths, and complete replay provenance.

## Execution limits

- QSA uses bounded gather/indexer chunks and native SDPA MATH. Dynamic selection shapes currently require disabling CUDA graphs; context parallelism is explicitly rejected.
- MTP training and speculative decoding are outside the port's current scope.
- Full 177B parameter materialization, production-scale convergence, and production throughput have not been validated.
- The pinned nightly has a preexisting CosSinRoPE eager/compile discrepancy on unchanged upstream/main: one BF16 gradient value differs by `9.54e-7`. The pinned CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2 supports the validated fused GDN backend; the optional cuDNN backend requires DSL 4.7.0.

## Draft follow-ups for current upstream/main

The two implementation commits were validated against the source base above. Latest upstream/main (`3f990a8e9` when this draft was prepared) merges without textual conflicts, but has since changed the compile configuration and loss contracts.

- [ ] Migrate the Flash-Next configuration and fixtures from `local_compile_regions` to `LocalCompileConfig`, following #5463, so the intended eager debug configuration is honored.
- [ ] Revalidate the integration fixtures and deterministic golden on current upstream/main, including the compile configuration update and loss abstraction redesign in #4582, before marking this PR ready for review.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates.

+#
+# This source code is licensed under the BSD-style license found in the
+# LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree.
+
+"""Same-weight component, block, vision and full-logit Flash-Next parity.
+
+Install transformers at 494470d677d05d44153d235d795e0d01040307ab, then run:
+python -m scripts.checkpoint_conversion.numerical_tests_qwen3_8_flash_next
+The reduced fixture retains every backbone feature. Components and gradients
+use FP32; the recurrent backbone uses BF16, as required by its shared kernel.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import copy
+import json
+from contextlib import ExitStack
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+from torch.nn.attention import sdpa_kernel, SDPBackend
+
+from torchtitan.config.parallelism import ParallelismConfig
+from torchtitan.models.qwen3_8_flash_next import build_model_config
+from torchtitan.models.qwen3_8_flash_next.state_dict_adapter import (
+    Qwen38FlashNextStateDictAdapter,
+)
+
+REFERENCE_REVISION = "494470d677d05d44153d235d795e0d01040307ab"
+CHECKPOINT_REVISION = "de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540"
+
+# T = packed tokens, D = model dimension, C = residual streams * D,
+# E = experts, K = selected experts, V = vocabulary.
+BF16_EPS = torch.finfo(torch.bfloat16).eps
+
+
+def reference_text_config() -> Any:
+    from transformers.models.qwen4_exp.configuration_qwen4_exp import Qwen4ExpTextConfig
+
+    return Qwen4ExpTextConfig(
+        hidden_size=256,
+        vocab_size=64,
+        num_hidden_layers=8,
+        num_attention_heads=4,
+        num_key_value_heads=2,
+        head_dim=64,
+        max_position_embeddings=64,
+        linear_num_key_heads=2,
+        linear_num_value_heads=4,
+        linear_key_head_dim=128,
+        linear_value_head_dim=128,
+        num_experts=8,
+        num_experts_per_tok=2,
+        moe_intermediate_size=128,
+        shared_expert_intermediate_size=128,
+        hc_count=4,
+        hc_lowrank=32,
+        ple_layer_ids=[2],
+        ple_embed_dim=256,
+        heads_per_ngram=2,
+        ngram_vocab_size_base=257,
+        split_ngram_parts=4,
+        eos_token_id=63,
+        indexer_n_heads=4,
+        indexer_kv_heads=1,
+        indexer_head_dim=64,
+        indexer_budget=16,
+        indexer_compress_ratio=4,
+        output_gate_type="sigmoid",
+        rope_parameters={
+            "rope_type": "default",
+            "rope_theta": 10_000_000,
+            "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25,
+            "mrope_section": [3, 3, 2],
+            "mrope_interleaved": True,
+        },
+        use_cache=False,
+    )
+
+
+def run(*, device: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    from transformers.models.qwen4_exp.configuration_qwen4_exp import (
+        Qwen4ExpVisionConfig,
+    )
+    from transformers.models.qwen4_exp.modeling_qwen4_exp import (
+        Qwen4ExpForCausalLM,
+        Qwen4ExpVisionModel,
+    )
+
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
+    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("highest")
+    torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False
+    config = build_model_config(
+        "debugmodel", seq_len=64, parallelism=ParallelismConfig()
+    )
+    vision_config = config.vision_encoder
+    assert vision_config is not None
+    config.vision_encoder = None
+    config.vocab_size = (
+        config.tok_embeddings.num_embeddings
+    ) = config.lm_head.out_features = 64
+    config.layers[1].ple.ple_embedding.vocab_size = 64
+    config.layers[1].ple.ple_embedding.eos_token_id = 63
+    hf_config = reference_text_config()
+    hf_config._attn_implementation = "sdpa"
+    hf = Qwen4ExpForCausalLM(hf_config).to(device).eval()
+    native = config.build().to(device).eval()
+    adapter = Qwen38FlashNextStateDictAdapter(config, None)
+    native.load_state_dict(adapter.from_hf(hf.state_dict()), strict=True)
+    positions = torch.arange(39, device=device)
+    tokens = torch.randint(0, 63, (39,), device=device)
+    tokens[7] = 63
+    hidden = torch.randn(39, 1024, device=device, requires_grad=True)
+    results: dict[str, Any] = {}
+
+    def compare(
+        name: str,
+        actual: torch.Tensor,
+        expected: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        atol: float = 2e-5,
+        rtol: float = 2e-5,
+    ) -> None:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            actual,
+            expected,
+            atol=atol,
+            rtol=rtol,
+            msg=lambda message: f"{name}: {message}",
+        )
+        difference = actual.detach().double() - expected.detach().double()
+        results[name] = {
+            "max_abs": float(difference.abs().max()),
+            "rms": float(difference.square().mean().sqrt()),
+            "relative_l2": float(difference.norm() / expected.detach().double().norm()),
+            "atol": atol,
+            "rtol": rtol,
+        }
+
+    def compare_gradients(
+        name: str,
+        actual_loss: torch.Tensor,
+        expected_loss: torch.Tensor,
+        input_TC: torch.Tensor,
+        actual_module: torch.nn.Module,
+        expected_module: torch.nn.Module,
+    ) -> None:
+        actual_parameters = dict(actual_module.named_parameters())
+        expected_parameters = dict(expected_module.named_parameters())
+        assert actual_parameters.keys() == expected_parameters.keys()
+        actual_grads = torch.autograd.grad(
+            actual_loss, (input_TC, *actual_parameters.values())
+        )
+        expected_grads = torch.autograd.grad(
+            expected_loss, (input_TC, *expected_parameters.values())
+        )
+        for field, actual_grad, expected_grad in zip(
+            ("input", *actual_parameters), actual_grads, expected_grads
+        ):
+            compare(
+                f"{name}_gradient/{field}",
+                actual_grad,

+"""GDN normalization policy across local, CP, and recomputed backward paths."""

+def _sum_kernel(q, k, v, g, beta, **kwargs):
+    return q + k + v + g.unsqueeze(-1) + beta.unsqueeze(-1), None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("deterministic", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", ["chunk", "recomputed_backward", "context_parallel"])
+def test_l2norm_backward_tuning_obeys_determinism(deterministic, path):
+    previous = torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled()
+    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(deterministic)
+    try:
+        q, k, v = (torch.ones(3, 2, 4) for _ in range(3))
+        g, beta = (torch.ones(3, 2) for _ in range(2))
+        offsets = torch.tensor([0, 1, 3], dtype=torch.int32)
+        with (
+            mock.patch.object(gdn, "require_attn_gym"),
+            mock.patch.object(cp_gdn, "require_attn_gym"),
+            mock.patch.object(gdn, "chunk_kernel_options", return_value=None),
+            mock.patch.object(gdn, "chunk_gdn", side_effect=_sum_kernel),
+            mock.patch.object(cp_gdn, "context_parallel_gdn", side_effect=_sum_kernel),
+            mock.patch.object(cp_gdn, "spmd_mesh_group", return_value=object()),
+            mock.patch.object(
+                gdn, "l2norm", side_effect=lambda x, **kwargs: x
+            ) as local_norm,
+            mock.patch.object(
+                cp_gdn, "l2norm", side_effect=lambda x, **kwargs: x
+            ) as cp_norm,
+        ):
+            if path == "chunk":
+                kernel = gdn.GDNKernel.Config().build()
+                kernel(q, k, v, g, beta, cu_seqlens=offsets)
+            elif path == "recomputed_backward":
+                inputs = tuple(x.unsqueeze(0) for x in (q, k, v, g, beta))
+                gradients = gdn._chunk_gdn_gradients(
+                    torch.ones_like(inputs[0]), *inputs, offsets
+                )
+                for gradient in gradients[:3]:
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(gradient, torch.ones_like(gradient))
+                for gradient in gradients[3:]:
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(gradient, torch.full_like(gradient, 4))
+            else:
+                inner = cp_gdn.ContextParallelInnerGDN.Config(
+                    conv_kernel_size=4, kernel=gdn.GDNKernel.Config()
+                ).build()
+                routing = cast(
+                    ContextParallelRouting, SimpleNamespace(cu_seqlens=offsets)
+                )
+                inner.gdn_core(q, k, v, g, beta, cu_seqlens=offsets, routing=routing)
+            normalizer = cp_norm if path == "context_parallel" else local_norm
+            assert normalizer.call_count == 2
+            for call in normalizer.call_args_list:
+                assert call.kwargs["autotune"] is (not deterministic)
+                assert call.kwargs["cu_seqlens"] is offsets
+    finally:
+        torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(previous)

+            query.dtype
+        )

+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=0, rtol=0)
+        upstream = torch.randn_like(actual)
+        actual_grad = torch.autograd.grad(

+    mask = (1 << 64) - 1

+        if position == 0:

+        context += [63] * (3 - len(context))

+            hashed = 0
+            for i in range(ngram):
+                hashed ^= (context[i] * int(embedding.layer_multipliers[i])) & mask
+            if hashed >= 1 << 63:
+                hashed -= 1 << 64
+            for head in range((ngram - 2) * 2, (ngram - 1) * 2):
+                row.append(
+                    hashed % int(embedding.ngram_heads_vocab_sizes[head])
+                    + int(embedding.ngram_heads_offsets[head])

+        expected.append(row)

+def test_qsa_selection_matches_document_local_block_oracle(config):

+    positions = torch.cat((torch.arange(19), torch.arange(20)))
+    padding = torch.zeros(39, dtype=torch.bool)
+    padding[5] = padding[37:] = True
+    selected, scores = indexer(
+        x, positions=positions, document_positions_T=positions, padding_mask_T=padding
+    )
+    projection = indexer.index_qk_proj(x)
+    queries = indexer._rotate(
+        indexer.q_layernorm(projection[:, :256].unflatten(-1, (4, 64))), positions
+    )
+    for query in range(39):
+        begin = 0 if query < 19 else 19
+        visible = (
+            [token for token in range(begin, query + 1) if not padding[token]]
+            if not padding[query]
+            else []
+        )
+        complete = len(visible) // 4
+        blocks = torch.tensor(visible[: complete * 4], dtype=torch.long).reshape(
+            complete, 4
+        )
+        pooled = projection[blocks, 256:].float().mean(1)
+        keys = indexer._rotate(
+            indexer.k_layernorm(pooled).unsqueeze(1), positions[blocks[:, 0]]
+        ).squeeze(1)
+        oracle_scores = (queries[query].float() @ keys.float().T).relu().sum(0) / 8
+        winners = oracle_scores.topk(min(4, complete)).indices
+        expected = [*blocks[winners].flatten().tolist(), *visible[complete * 4 :]]
+        actual = selected[query][selected[query] >= 0].tolist()
+        assert set(actual) == set(expected)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(

+def test_router_bfloat16_ties_mixing_and_backward(config):
+    """Round before expert selection and retain differentiable normalized gates."""
+    router = config.layers[3].feed_forward.router.build().bfloat16().eval()
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        router.gate.weight.zero_()
+        router.gate.weight[0, :2] = torch.tensor([1.0, 1 / 256])
+        router.gate.weight[1, 0] = 1
+        router.gate.weight[2, :2] = torch.tensor([1.0, 1 / 256])
+    x = torch.ones(3, 256, dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+    reference_weight = router.gate.weight.detach().float().requires_grad_()
+    reference_x = x.detach().float().requires_grad_()
+    logits = F.linear(reference_x, reference_weight).to(x.dtype).float()
+    reference_scores, reference_ids = logits.softmax(-1).topk(2, -1)
+    reference_scores = (reference_scores / reference_scores.sum(-1, keepdim=True)).to(
+        x.dtype
+    )
+    scores, indices, routing = router(x)
+    expected_routing = torch.zeros_like(logits, dtype=torch.bool).scatter(
+        -1, reference_ids, True
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(routing, expected_routing)
+    assert not torch.equal(
+        indices.sort(-1).values,
+        F.linear(reference_x, reference_weight).topk(2, -1).indices.sort(-1).values,
+    )
+    actual_weights = torch.zeros_like(logits).scatter(-1, indices, scores.float())
+    expected_weights = torch.zeros_like(logits).scatter(
+        -1, reference_ids, reference_scores.float()
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_weights, expected_weights, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    objective = torch.arange(8, dtype=torch.float32)
+    actual_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
+        (actual_weights * objective).sum(), (x, router.gate.weight)
+    )
+    expected_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
+        (expected_weights * objective).sum(), (reference_x, reference_weight)
+    )
+    for actual_grad, expected_grad in zip(actual_gradients, expected_gradients):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            actual_grad.float(), expected_grad.to(x.dtype).float(), atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-2
+        )
+

+    from torchtitan.models.qwen3_8_flash_next.model import Qwen38FlashNextModel

+            for _ in range(2):
+                output = model(
+                    ids, positions=positions, aux_loss_denominators=torch.tensor([46.0])
+                )
+                accumulated = [loss.instance_acc.clone() for loss in losses]
+                output.square().mean().backward()
+                for loss, expected in zip(losses, accumulated):
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(

+            optimizer.step()
+            assert AuxLoss.group_acc[("loss", "qsa_indexer_loss")] == 0
+    finally:
+        AuxLoss._group_counts.clear()
+        AuxLoss._group_counts.update(saved_counts)
+        AuxLoss.group_acc.clear()
+        AuxLoss.group_acc.update(saved_acc)

+# Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
+
+This package implements the released text and vision backbone of
+[Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), following
+the `add_model` workflow in [PR #5636](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5636).
+The checkpoint revision is `de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540`.
+The reference is Transformers' `Qwen4Exp` implementation at
+`494470d677d05d44153d235d795e0d01040307ab`.
+
+## Architecture
+
+Compared with the existing Qwen3.8 MoE port, Flash-Next adds four gated residual
+streams, per-layer lexical embeddings (PLE), and Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA).
+It reuses Qwen3.5's Gated DeltaNet, MoE, multimodal preprocessing, MRoPE, vision
+encoder, checkpoint conversion, and training lifecycle.
+
+| Component | Released configuration |
+| --- | --- |
+| Decoder | 48 layers, dimension 2560, three GDN layers per QSA layer |
+| Residual streams | Four, grouped offset RMSNorm, mixing rank 320 |
+| QSA | 24 query heads, 2 KV heads, dimension 256, rotary dimension 64 |
+| Indexer | Four query heads, one KV head, dimension 128, compress ratio 4 |
+| Selection | Top 512 complete blocks (2048 tokens), plus the current partial block |
+| MoE | 512 experts, top 10, dimension 640, one gated shared expert |
+| GDN | 16 key heads, 48 value heads, key/value dimension 128, sigmoid output gate |
+| PLE | Decoder layer 2, bigram/trigram hashes, 16 hash heads, dimension 2560 |
+| PLE table | 320001536 rows x 160 features, 128 HF checkpoint chunks |
+| Vision | 27 layers, dimension 1152, 16 heads, patch size 16, temporal patch size 2 |
+| Vocabulary | 248320, EOS 248044 |
+
+The `125B-A6B` flavor follows the release's size label. Meta construction counts
+177392830576 native parameters, including 51200245760 lexical table parameters
+and 448931056 vision parameters. The reference excludes the MTP draft head:
+the adapter loads all 1627 backbone/vision checkpoint entries and warns when it
+encounters the 31 unused `mtp.*` entries. MTP training and speculative decoding
+are outside this port's scope.
+
+QSA pools raw indexer keys before normalization and rotary embedding. Selection
+respects document boundaries, padding, and causality. Its training objective
+uses the technical report's sparse-stage KL target: sum the detached main
+attention probabilities over heads, max-pool each complete block, and normalize
+over the selected blocks. Heads are summed across TP before max pooling. The
+report does not specify its coefficient; the flavor uses `1.0`, independently
+of the MoE load-balancing coefficient `0.001`.
+
+PLE hashes reset at EOS and packed document boundaries. Its dilated causal
+convolution resets at document boundaries. Original token IDs and document
+positions travel to later pipeline stages separately from multimodal rotary
+coordinates. The lexical table uses TP across features so exporting the HF row
+chunks preserves sharding without gathering the full table on every rank.
+
+## Usage
+
+```python
+import torch
+from torchtitan.config.parallelism import ParallelismConfig
+from torchtitan.models.qwen3_8_flash_next import build_model_config
+
+config = build_model_config(
+    "125B-A6B", seq_len=4096, parallelism=ParallelismConfig()
+)
+with torch.device("meta"):
+    model = config.build()
+```
+
+The reduced `debugmodel` retains GDN, QSA, GR, PLE, MoE, and optional vision.
+Importable training fixtures live in

+## Numerical evidence
+
+The reproducible same-weight reference harness is

+| Comparison | Maximum absolute error |
+| --- | --- |
+| GR read/write, input and parameter gradients, FP32 | 0 |
+| PLE forward, FP32 | 7.45e-9 |
+| PLE input and parameter gradients, FP32 | 3.19e-12 |
+| QSA forward, FP32 | 4.10e-8 |
+| Vision including merger, FP32 | 3.28e-7 |

+half-epsilon absolute tolerance plus one epsilon relative tolerance; the FP32
+checks cover operation-order rounding. New CPU tests also use independent
+functional oracles for GR, hashing, PLE convolution, selected attention, KL,
+router rounding, gradients, packed inputs, and optimizer/remat resets.

+two near-tied tokens change expert sets in this fixture, giving an unconstrained
+maximum logit difference of `0.02587890625`. Replaying only the isolated expert
+IDs and recomputing the packed mixing weights reduces it to `0.00390625`.

+for unconstrained BF16 routing. CPU boundary tests check the math independently.

+## Execution limits
+
+QSA currently uses bounded indexer/gather chunks and native SDPA MATH. CUDA
+graphs are disabled in the fixtures because block selection has dynamic shapes;
+context parallelism is rejected explicitly. The complete released checkpoint
+schema is checked on meta tensors and reduced checkpoints load strictly, but
+full 177B parameter materialization and production-scale convergence have not
+been validated. The reduced-model runs establish correctness and training
+behavior, and do not establish production throughput.

+"""Qwen Sparse Attention with complete-block selection and indexer distillation."""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+import torch_remat as remat
+from torch.distributed._functional_collectives import all_reduce, wait_tensor
+from torch.nn.attention import sdpa_kernel, SDPBackend
+
+from torchtitan.distributed.spmd_types import spmd_mesh_group, spmd_mesh_size
+from torchtitan.models.base.module import Module
+from torchtitan.models.common import Linear
+from torchtitan.models.common.attention import (
+    InnerAttention,
+    local_head_split,
+    VarlenAttentionMetadata,
+)
+from torchtitan.models.common.attention.attention import (
+    create_varlen_metadata_for_document,
+)
+from torchtitan.models.common.aux_loss import AuxLoss
+from torchtitan.models.common.linear import maybe_gather_tp_input
+from torchtitan.models.qwen3_5.model import OffsetRMSNorm, Qwen35Attention
+from torchtitan.models.qwen3_5.rope import MRoPE
+
+from .embedding import document_starts
+
+# T = packed tokens, U = valid tokens, G = complete blocks, R = block size,
+# B = selected blocks, J = selected tokens including the incomplete tail,
+# H = query or KV heads, K = head dimension, V = value dimension,
+# D = model dimension, Q = query chunk, C = projection channels.
+
+
+class QSAIndexer(Module):
+    """Score average-pooled complete blocks; always keep the incomplete tail."""
+
+    @dataclass(kw_only=True, slots=True)
+    class Config(Module.Config):
+        num_heads: int
+        head_dim: int
+        rotary_dim: int
+        token_budget: int
+        compress_ratio: int
+        index_qk_proj: Linear.Config
+        q_layernorm: OffsetRMSNorm.Config
+        k_layernorm: OffsetRMSNorm.Config
+        rope: MRoPE.Config
+        chunk_size: int = 128
+
+        def __post_init__(self):
+            if (
+                min(self.num_heads, self.head_dim, self.compress_ratio, self.chunk_size)
+                <= 0
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "Indexer head counts, dimensions and chunk sizes must be positive"
+                )
+            if (
+                self.token_budget < self.compress_ratio
+                or self.token_budget % self.compress_ratio
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "token_budget must be a positive multiple of compress_ratio"
+                )
+            if not 0 < self.rotary_dim <= self.head_dim or self.rotary_dim % 2:
+                raise ValueError("rotary_dim must be positive, even and <= head_dim")
+
+    def __init__(self, config: Config):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.num_heads = config.num_heads
+        self.head_dim = config.head_dim
+        self.rotary_dim = config.rotary_dim
+        self.compress_ratio = config.compress_ratio
+        self.block_topk = config.token_budget // config.compress_ratio
+        self.chunk_size = config.chunk_size
+        self.index_qk_proj = config.index_qk_proj.build()
+        self.q_layernorm = config.q_layernorm.build()
+        self.k_layernorm = config.k_layernorm.build()
+        self.rope = config.rope.build()
+
+    def _rotate(self, x_THK: torch.Tensor, positions_T: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        rotary_THR = x_THK[..., : self.rotary_dim]
+        rotary_THR, _ = self.rope(rotary_THR, rotary_THR, positions_T)
+        return torch.cat((rotary_THR, x_THK[..., self.rotary_dim :]), -1)
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        x_TD: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        document_positions_T: torch.Tensor,
+        padding_mask_T: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        num_tokens = x_TD.shape[0]
+        qk_TC = self.index_qk_proj(x_TD)
+        remat.recompute_needs_tensor(qk_TC)
+        query_TC, raw_key_TK = qk_TC.split(
+            (self.num_heads * self.head_dim, self.head_dim), -1
+        )
+        query_THK = self._rotate(
+            self.q_layernorm(query_TC.unflatten(-1, (self.num_heads, self.head_dim))),
+            positions,
+        )
+        indices_T = torch.arange(num_tokens, device=x_TD.device)
+        starts_T = document_starts(document_positions_T)
+        valid_T = (
+            torch.ones_like(indices_T, dtype=torch.bool)
+            if padding_mask_T is None
+            else ~padding_mask_T
+        )
+        counts_T = valid_T.long().cumsum(0)
+        start_counts_T = F.pad(counts_T[:-1], (1, 0))[starts_T]
+        local_counts_T = counts_T - start_counts_T
+        valid_indices_U = valid_T.nonzero().flatten()
+        block_ends_G = (
+            (valid_T & (local_counts_T.remainder(self.compress_ratio) == 0))
+            .nonzero()
+            .flatten()
+        )
+        block_indices_GR = valid_indices_U[
+            counts_T[block_ends_G, None]
+            - self.compress_ratio
+            + torch.arange(self.compress_ratio, device=x_TD.device)
+        ]
+        pooled_GK = raw_key_TK[block_indices_GR].float().mean(1).to(raw_key_TK.dtype)
+        key_GK = self._rotate(
+            self.k_layernorm(pooled_GK).unsqueeze(1), positions[block_indices_GR[:, 0]]
+        ).squeeze(1)
+        num_selected = min(self.block_topk, block_ends_G.numel())
+        tail_count_T = local_counts_T.remainder(self.compress_ratio)
+        tail_offsets_TR = torch.arange(
+            self.compress_ratio - 1, device=x_TD.device
+        ).expand(num_tokens, -1)
+        tail_slots_TR = counts_T[:, None] - tail_count_T[:, None] + tail_offsets_TR
+        # The extra entry makes all-padding documents a well-defined empty selection.
+        tail_indices_TR = F.pad(valid_indices_U, (0, 1))[
+            tail_slots_TR.clamp_max(valid_indices_U.numel())
+        ]
+        tail_indices_TR = tail_indices_TR.masked_fill(
+            ~(valid_T[:, None] & (tail_offsets_TR < tail_count_T[:, None])), -1
+        )
+        selected_indices = []
+        selected_scores = []
+        for start in range(0, num_tokens, self.chunk_size):
+            stop = start + self.chunk_size
+            scores_QHG = torch.einsum(
+                "qhk,gk->qhg", query_THK[start:stop].float(), key_GK.float()
+            )
+            scores_QG = scores_QHG.relu().sum(1) * self.head_dim**-0.5
+            visible_QG = (
+                (block_ends_G[None] <= indices_T[start:stop, None])
+                & (starts_T[block_ends_G][None] == starts_T[start:stop, None])
+                & valid_T[start:stop, None]
+            )
+            scores_QB, blocks_QB = scores_QG.masked_fill(~visible_QG, -torch.inf).topk(
+                num_selected, -1
+            )
+            tokens_QBR = block_indices_GR[blocks_QB].masked_fill(
+                ~scores_QB.isfinite().unsqueeze(-1), -1
+            )
+            selected_indices.append(
+                torch.cat(
+                    (tokens_QBR.flatten(-2), tail_indices_TR[start:stop]), -1
+                ).int()
+            )
+            selected_scores.append(scores_QB)
+        return torch.cat(selected_indices), torch.cat(selected_scores)
+
+
+class QSAIndexerLoss(AuxLoss):
+    """KL loss on selected complete blocks from the report's sparse training stage."""
+
+    @dataclass(kw_only=True, slots=True)
+    class Config(AuxLoss.Config):
+        pass
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def block_kl(scores_QB: torch.Tensor, teacher_QB: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        valid_QB = scores_QB.isfinite()
+        log_probs_QB = F.log_softmax(
+            scores_QB.masked_fill(~valid_QB, torch.finfo(torch.float32).min), -1
+        )
+        teacher_QB = teacher_QB.detach() * valid_QB
+        teacher_QB = teacher_QB / teacher_QB.sum(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-30)
+        return (torch.xlogy(teacher_QB, teacher_QB) - teacher_QB * log_probs_QB).sum()
+
+
+class QSAInnerAttention(InnerAttention):
+    """Selected-token SDPA with bounded gathers and a detached attention teacher."""
+
+    @dataclass(kw_only=True, slots=True)
+    class Config(InnerAttention.Config):
+        compress_ratio: int
+        num_heads: int
+        indexer_loss: QSAIndexerLoss.Config
+        chunk_size: int = 16
+
+        @property
+        def is_full_attention(self) -> bool:
+            return True
+
+        def build_attention_metadata(
+            self, positions, **kwargs
+        ) -> VarlenAttentionMetadata:
+            return create_varlen_metadata_for_document(positions, **kwargs)
+
+    def __init__(self, config: Config):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.compress_ratio = config.compress_ratio
+        self.num_heads = config.num_heads
+        self.chunk_size = config.chunk_size
+        self.indexer_loss = config.indexer_loss.build()
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        query_THK: torch.Tensor,
+        key_THK: torch.Tensor,
+        value_THV: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        selected_indices_TJ: torch.Tensor,
+        scores_TB: torch.Tensor,
+        scale: float,
+        enable_gqa: bool,
+        aux_loss_denominator: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        train_indexer = self.training and self.indexer_loss.coeff != 0
+        if train_indexer and aux_loss_denominator is None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "QSA training requires the step-global auxiliary-loss denominator"
+            )
+        num_blocks = scores_TB.shape[-1]
+        outputs = []
+        raw_sum = scores_TB.new_zeros(())
+        for start in range(0, query_THK.shape[0], self.chunk_size):
+            stop = start + self.chunk_size
+            indices_QJ = selected_indices_TJ[start:stop].long()
+            valid_QJ = indices_QJ >= 0
+            query_QH1K = query_THK[start:stop].unsqueeze(2)
+            keys_QHJK = key_THK[indices_QJ.clamp_min(0)].transpose(1, 2)
+            values_QHJV = value_THV[indices_QJ.clamp_min(0)].transpose(1, 2)
+            with sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.MATH):
+                output_QHV = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
+                    query_QH1K,
+                    keys_QHJK,
+                    values_QHJV,
+                    attn_mask=valid_QJ[:, None, None],
+                    scale=scale,
+                    enable_gqa=enable_gqa,
+                ).squeeze(2)
+            outputs.append(output_QHV)
+            if train_indexer and num_blocks:
+                with torch.no_grad():
+                    keys_QHJK = keys_QHJK.repeat_interleave(
+                        query_QH1K.shape[1] // keys_QHJK.shape[1], 1
+                    )
+                    logits_QHJ = (query_QH1K.float() * keys_QHJK.float()).sum(
+                        -1
+                    ) * scale
+                    logits_QHJ = logits_QHJ.masked_fill(
+                        ~valid_QJ[:, None], torch.finfo(torch.float32).min
+                    )
+                    teacher_QJ = logits_QHJ.softmax(-1).sum(1) / self.num_heads
+                    teacher_QJ = teacher_QJ * valid_QJ
+                    tp_group = spmd_mesh_group("tp")
+                    if tp_group is not None:
+                        teacher_QJ = wait_tensor(
+                            all_reduce(teacher_QJ, "sum", tp_group)
+                        )
+                    # Sum heads before max pooling; pooling each TP shard first
+                    # changes the target distribution.
+                    teacher_QB = (
+                        teacher_QJ[:, : num_blocks * self.compress_ratio]
+                        .unflatten(-1, (num_blocks, self.compress_ratio))
+                        .amax(-1)
+                    )
+                raw_sum = raw_sum + self.indexer_loss.block_kl(
+                    scores_TB[start:stop], teacher_QB
+                )
+        output_THV = torch.cat(outputs)
+        if train_indexer:
+            # Indexer parameters and scores are TP-replicated. The FSDP bridge
+            # sums their local gradients, so contribute the global KL once.
+            raw_sum = raw_sum.detach() + (raw_sum - raw_sum.detach()) / spmd_mesh_size(
+                "tp"
+            )
+            output_THV = self.indexer_loss.inject(
+                raw_sum,
+                carrier=output_THV,
+                denominator=aux_loss_denominator,
+            )
+        return output_THV
+
+
+class QSAAttention(Qwen35Attention):
+    """Qwen3.5's gated QK-normalized attention with the Flash-Next indexer."""
+
+    @dataclass(kw_only=True, slots=True)
+    class Config(Qwen35Attention.Config):
+        indexer: QSAIndexer.Config
+
+    def __init__(self, config: Config):
+        super().__init__(config)
+        self.indexer = config.indexer.build()
+
+    def forward(  # pyrefly: ignore [bad-override]
+        self,
+        x_TD: torch.Tensor,
+        attention_metadata: VarlenAttentionMetadata | None,
+        positions: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        *,
+        document_positions_T: torch.Tensor,
+        padding_mask_T: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        aux_loss_denominator: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        del attention_metadata
+        if positions is None:
+            raise ValueError("QSA requires explicit rotary positions")
+        x_TD = maybe_gather_tp_input(self, x_TD)
+        selected_indices_TJ, scores_TB = self.indexer(
+            x_TD,
+            positions=positions,
+            document_positions_T=document_positions_T,
+            padding_mask_T=padding_mask_T,
+        )
+        query_gate_THC = local_head_split(
+            self.wq(x_TD), self.head_dim * 2, cp_shard_dim=0
+        )
+        query_THK, gate_THV = query_gate_THC.chunk(2, -1)
+        key_THK = local_head_split(self.wk(x_TD), self.head_dim, cp_shard_dim=0)
+        value_THV = local_head_split(self.wv(x_TD), self.head_dim, cp_shard_dim=0)
+        remat.recompute_needs_tensor(query_THK, key_THK)
+        query_THK, key_THK = self._partial_rope(
+            self.q_norm(query_THK), self.k_norm(key_THK), positions
+        )
+        output_THV = remat.region(
+            self.inner_attention,
+            self.remat_region_name("inner_attention"),
+            recompute=self.remat_should_recompute("inner_attention"),
+        )(
+            query_THK,
+            key_THK,
+            value_THV,
+            selected_indices_TJ=selected_indices_TJ,
+            scores_TB=scores_TB,
+            scale=self.scaling,
+            enable_gqa=self.enable_gqa,
+            aux_loss_denominator=aux_loss_denominator,
+        )
+        remat.recompute_needs_tensor(output_THV, gate_THV)
+        output_TD = (output_THV * gate_THV.sigmoid()).flatten(-2)
+        return self.wo(output_TD)

+"""Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's hybrid multimodal decoder."""
+

+from torch import nn

+from torchtitan.distributed.spmd_types import (

+from torchtitan.models.common.flops import (
